hypotheses.text: The core published clinical cohort of FILIP1-related neuromuscular disorder with dysmorphic facies across seminal peer-reviewed discovery papers consists of exactly 10 detailed individuals from two primary cohorts (Schnabel et al. 2023, n=5; Roos et al. 2023, n=5), across which dysmorphic facial features and muscle weakness exhibit a penetrance of 100% (10/10).
hypotheses.rationale: Pinning down the exact universal denominator (n=10) and cross-cohort baseline frequencies prevents inflated or distorted clinical penetrance estimates when establishing diagnostic criteria.

evidence.text: Schnabel et al. reported five affected individuals from three independent families with homozygous truncating FILIP1 variants, all sharing contractures, microcephaly, and facial dysmorphism.

source.title: Homozygous loss-of-function variants in FILIP1 cause autosomal recessive arthrogryposis multiplex congenita with microcephaly
source.quote: Here, we report five affected individuals from three independent families sharing an overlapping phenotype with congenital contractures affecting shoulder, elbow, hand, hip, knee and foot as well as scoliosis, reduced palmar and plantar skin folds, microcephaly and facial dysmorphism.

evidence.text: Roos et al. described five patients from four unrelated consanguineous families harboring homozygous FILIP1 variants (two nonsense, two missense) showing muscle weakness, pathology, neurodevelopmental delay, and dysmorphic features.

source.title: Bi-allelic variants of FILIP1 cause congenital myopathy, dysmorphism and neurological defects
source.quote: Here, we report on five patients from four unrelated consanguineous families with homozygous FILIP1 variants (two nonsense and two missense)... Patients exhibit a broad spectrum of neurological symptoms including brain malformations, neurodevelopmental delay, muscle weakness and pathology and dysmorphic features.

hypotheses.text: Reduced palmar and plantar skin folds represent an obligate cutaneous marker (5/5, 100%) in patients with homozygous truncating FILIP1 loss-of-function variants presenting with arthrogryposis multiplex congenita, distinguishing them from classic congenital myopathies without distal skin crease obliteration.
hypotheses.rationale: If reduced or absent palmar/plantar creases correlate strictly with the prenatal akinesia and joint immobilization seen in severe truncating variants, this serves as an immediate physical sign accessible to the clinician.

evidence.text: All five individuals reported by Schnabel et al. presented with reduced palmar and plantar skin folds alongside generalized joint contractures and microcephaly.

source.title: Homozygous loss-of-function variants in FILIP1 cause autosomal recessive arthrogryposis multiplex congenita with microcephaly
source.quote: sharing an overlapping phenotype with congenital contractures affecting shoulder, elbow, hand, hip, knee and foot as well as scoliosis, reduced palmar and plantar skin folds, microcephaly and facial dysmorphism.

hypotheses.text: Homozygous structural copy-number losses (autosomal deletions) in FILIP1 account for an under-recognized proportion of syndromic arthrogryposis and microcephaly diagnoses in highly consanguineous or resource-limited cohorts.
hypotheses.rationale: Testing whether non-exonic/structural deletions of FILIP1 represent a distinct mutational mechanism beyond SNVs expands the denominator of affected individuals and informs which genetic assay to select.

evidence.text: Chaurasia et al. identified biallelic FILIP1 variants causing syndromic arthrogryposis through systematic analysis of rare homozygous copy number losses in exome data from an Indian cohort of 2021 individuals.

source.title: Systematic analysis of homozygous autosomal copy number losses in exomes improves diagnostic yield and uncovers ultra-rare recessive disorders
source.quote: Further analysis of the data and identification of additional affected individuals through collaboration led to identification of biallelic FILIP1 and FAM177A1 variants as causes of a syndromic arthrogryposis and a neuromuscular disorder respectively.

new_directions.question_text: What are the exact clinical and dysmorphic features documented in the FILIP1 deletion cases identified by Chaurasia et al. (2026), and do their individual phenotypes match the Schnabel (2023) truncating AMC phenotype?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifies whether homozygous copy number deletions mirror the complete loss-of-function AMC/microcephaly presentation of truncating SNVs and adds exact patient numbers to the global denominator.

new_directions.question_text: What is the per-patient presence or absence of microcephaly versus normal head circumference across the missense subset in the Roos et al. (2023) cohort?
new_directions.rationale: Directly verifies whether microcephaly has 100% penetrance across all variant classes or is restricted solely to complete loss-of-function/truncating alleles.
